theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: As team leader, you must order the steel for a set of balcony rails. Which is the best starting point?
options: Last month's order, copied with the same quantities
The checked drawings and a cutting list made from them
The supplier's newest price list and its special offers
A rough guess from the welder who built the last rail

questions.stem: Why do you plan how the pieces on a cutting list will come out of standard 6 m lengths before you order?
options: So the supplier will cut every piece to size for free
So every offcut can be thrown out the same day
So the welders know which pieces to weld first
To order the fewest lengths with little waste

options: To show the supplier where to stamp the grade
To make the plate lighter for the team to carry

questions.stem: The specified grade of 6 mm plate is out of stock, and the supplier offers a different grade. What should you do?
options: Accept it, as all 6 mm plate is the same
Get approval from the engineer or person in charge

questions.stem: Why is a waste allowance added to the steel worked out from a cutting list?
options: So the welders can take some home
So the supplier can deliver a bit less
So the order is quicker to write out
To allow for cuts, offcuts and errors

questions.stem: A job needs 46 m² of mesh. Mesh comes in sheets 2.4 m × 1.2 m. Allowing 10% for waste, how many sheets are needed?
Why must grinding discs be ordered in the right size and with the right maximum speed for the shop's grinders?
options: So they match the colours used in the shop
So they can be used as cutting discs as well

So that the discs will last for a whole year

questions.stem: Why should the order file show which supplier, batch and date each lot of electrodes came from?
options: So the Centre can boast about its suppliers
So the welders know which box is the newest

So the boxes can be sent back when empty

questions.stem: When is the best time for a team leader to order the steel for a job?
options: Once the drawings and cutting list are checked
Before the client has agreed to the job at all
On the morning the welders are due to start
After the job is done, to restock the store

questions.stem: A supplier offers a 10% discount if you buy a whole year's stock of welding wire now. What should you think about first?
options: Whether the supplier's sales rep is friendly
Whether the boxes will look good on the shelf
Whether the discount is printed in colour

questions.stem: Some special steels must be imported into Jamaica. Which extra costs should be added when comparing an imported price?
options: The cost of painting the steel once it arrives
Freight, customs duty and clearing charges

options: Steel is always cheaper during the season
Suppliers close for the whole of the season

questions.stem: Why must an order for steel pipe give the outside diameter, the wall thickness or schedule, and the grade?
options: So the pipe arrives in the right colour
So it can be delivered more quickly

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What is the name of the list that gives every piece to be cut for a job, with its section, length and number off?
What figure, in kilograms per cubic metre, is normally used for the density of steel in mass calculations?
What document does a supplier send to show it has accepted your order, with the items, prices and delivery date?
A flat bar weighs 7.85 kg per metre. What is the mass of a 2.4 m length, in kg, to one decimal place?
A packet of electrodes costs J$5,200 before GCT. How much do 6 packets cost before GCT, in J$?
What do we call stock that has sat unused for a long time and is unlikely ever to be used?
What is the name of the regular charge a gas supplier makes for each cylinder the customer keeps?

What is the name of a request sent to several suppliers asking each to give its price for the same items?

What is the name of the government charge paid when goods are brought into Jamaica through customs?
A steel beam costs J$9,800 per metre. How much do 7.5 m cost, in J$?
Before a new supplier may be used, it is vetted and added to a register kept by the office. What is that register usually called?

essays.stem: Explain how you would work out the full list of materials to order for a steel gate and fence job from its drawings, including steel, consumables and finishing materials.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with the checked drawings and make a cutting list: every piece with its section size, length and number off. I group the pieces by section and plan how they come out of standard 6 m lengths, allowing for saw cuts, so I know how many lengths to order. For plate parts I nest them on a sketch of a full sheet to find the number of sheets. I add a waste allowance for offcuts and mistakes, often about 5 to 10 percent, or what the shop's records show. I list bought items such as hinges, bolts, locks and anchors. For consumables I estimate the weld metal from the weld sizes and lengths, divide by the deposit efficiency to get the electrodes or wire, and add grinding and cutting discs and gas. For finishing I work out the surface area and use the paint's coverage to find the litres of primer and topcoat. Finally I check what is already in the store and order only the balance.
markingPoints: Makes a cutting list from checked drawings
Plans cuts from stock lengths and nests plate
Adds a sensible waste allowance and lists bought items
Estimates consumables and paint by calculation
Checks existing stock and orders only what is needed

essays.stem: Explain how you would get and compare quotations for a large steel order and choose the supplier. Say why the lowest price is not always the best choice.
essays.modelAnswer: I send the same written request for quotation to three approved suppliers, with a full description of each item, the quantities, any certificates needed, the delivery address and the date needed. When the quotations come back, I put them side by side on a sheet. I compare the price of each item, the delivery charges, GCT at the current rate, any discounts, the delivery time, the payment terms and how long the price is valid. I check that each supplier is quoting exactly what was asked, with the right grade and mill certificates. The lowest price is not always best, because a cheap supplier may deliver late, send the wrong grade, have no certificates, or add charges later, and a late delivery can stop the job and cost more than the saving. I also think about each supplier's past record. I choose the best value, record why, and get the order approved by the person with authority.
markingPoints: Sends the same full request to several approved suppliers
Compares price, delivery charges, GCT, discounts, lead time and terms
Checks each quote meets the specification and certificates
Explains why the lowest price may not be best value
Records the choice and gets approval

essays.stem: Explain why every order line must describe the material fully. Give the details you would state for steel plate, hollow section, pipe, electrodes and a gas.
essays.modelAnswer: If an order is not complete, the supplier has to guess, and the wrong item may arrive. That wastes time, stops the job and can mean the work does not meet the design. For plate I state the thickness, the sheet size, the grade, the number of sheets and whether mill certificates are needed. For hollow section I state the shape, for example SHS or RHS, the outside sizes, the wall thickness, the grade, the length of each piece and the number of lengths. For pipe I state the outside diameter or nominal size, the wall thickness or schedule, the material grade, whether it is black or galvanised, the ends and the lengths. For electrodes I state the classification, such as E7018, the diameter, the packet size, the number of packets and that batch numbers must be shown. For a gas I state the exact gas or mixture, the cylinder size and the number of cylinders to exchange.
markingPoints: Explains the cost of an incomplete order
Plate: thickness, size, grade, quantity and certificates
Hollow section: shape, sizes, wall, grade, length and quantity
Pipe: diameter, wall or schedule, grade, finish and ends
Electrodes and gas: classification or mixture, size, quantity and batch or cylinder details

essays.stem: Your team has a six-week fabrication job that needs some imported fittings. Explain how you would plan the timing of all the orders so that work is never held up.
essays.modelAnswer: I start from the job programme, which shows when each stage starts: cutting, fabrication, welding, painting and installation. For each material I find out the lead time from the supplier, including freight and customs clearance for the imported fittings. I work backwards from the date each item is needed to find the latest date to order, and add a few days of safety time, more for imported items because shipping and customs can be delayed. The imported fittings are ordered first, on the day the job is confirmed. Steel for the first stage is ordered so that it arrives just before cutting starts, and later items, such as paint, are timed to arrive later, so the yard does not fill up and paint does not go past its shelf life. I put all the order and delivery dates on a simple chart, check with suppliers before each date, and tell the supervisor at once if anything is likely to be late, so the work can be re-planned.
markingPoints: Uses the job programme to find when each item is needed
Finds lead times, including freight and customs for imports
Works back to latest order dates with safety time
Orders long-lead items first and times others to avoid crowding or expiry
Tracks dates, follows up and reports likely delays early

essays.stem: Explain how you would set up stock control for welding consumables in the Centre's store. Include how you would work out a reorder level, with an example.
essays.modelAnswer: I list every consumable kept in stock, such as electrodes of each type and size, wire, discs and gas. Each item gets a bin card or a line in a spreadsheet showing stock in, stock out and the balance, and every issue is recorded against a job. Stock is used first in, first out, so older packets are used before newer ones and nothing goes past its shelf life. For each item I set a reorder level: the usage during the lead time plus a safety stock. For example, if the shop uses 15 kg of E7018 electrodes a week, delivery takes 2 weeks and I want 10 kg as safety stock, the reorder level is 15 × 2 + 10 = 40 kg. When the balance drops to 40 kg, I raise an order. I also set a maximum so that we do not overstock. Every month or term a stocktake compares the real stock with the records, and differences are investigated.
markingPoints: Records every item with stock in, out and balance
Uses first in, first out and watches shelf life
Explains reorder level as usage in lead time plus safety stock
Gives a correct worked example
Sets a maximum and does regular stocktakes

essays.stem: Describe how you would receive a steel delivery for a job that must meet a code, from the truck arriving to the steel being stored.
essays.modelAnswer: I make sure the unloading area is clear and that safe lifting equipment and trained people are ready. Before signing anything I check the delivery note against our purchase order. I count the lengths and sheets and measure sizes and thicknesses with a tape and vernier. I check the condition: no bends, deep pitting or damage. I check that the heat numbers stamped or painted on the steel match the mill certificates, and that the certificates show the grade ordered. Any shortage, wrong size, damage or missing certificate is written on the delivery note before I sign, and those items are refused or quarantined and reported. I then fill in a goods received note and book the steel into the stock records against the job. The steel is stored on racks off the ground, labelled with the job number and heat number and kept apart from general stock, so it can be traced. The certificates go into the job file.
markingPoints: Prepares a safe unloading area
Checks the delivery note against the order, counts and measures
Matches heat numbers to mill certificates and grade
Records problems before signing; quarantines and reports
Books in, labels, stores apart and files certificates for traceability

essays.stem: Explain how you would cost a materials order and keep it within the budget for a job.
essays.modelAnswer: I start with the budget for materials that was set when the job was priced. From the materials list I get prices from approved suppliers for each item, in J$. I multiply each price by the quantity and add the delivery charges, any freight, duty and clearing for imports, and GCT at the current rate where it applies. I take off any discounts. I compare the total with the budget. If it is over, I look for savings that do not lower the quality: better cutting plans to cut waste, using offcuts in the store, a cheaper approved supplier, or changing delivery to avoid charges. Any change to a specified material must be approved first. If the order is still over budget, I tell the supervisor before ordering, because only they can agree to spend more. I make sure the order is approved by someone with the right authority, and I keep a record of the costs so the actual spend can be compared with the budget at the end.
markingPoints: Starts from the job's materials budget
Prices each item and adds delivery, import costs and GCT at the current rate
Compares with the budget and looks for savings without lowering quality
Reports any overspend before ordering and gets proper approval
Records costs for comparison at the end

essays.stem: Explain the rules a team leader should follow when ordering materials for the Centre, and why each rule matters.
essays.modelAnswer: A team leader must only order within the limit of their authority, and get approval for anything above it, because this controls spending and stops wrong orders. Orders should go to approved suppliers and be chosen fairly on value, with quotations kept, so the choice can be shown to be honest. The leader must not accept gifts, money or favours from suppliers, and must declare any family or business link with a supplier, because these can bias the choice and are a form of corruption. Orders must be written, numbered and recorded, so that deliveries and invoices can be matched and checked. Orders should not be split to get under an approval limit. Materials belong to the Centre and must only be used for its jobs. Prices and supplier information are kept confidential. Following these rules protects the Centre's money, keeps trust with suppliers and protects the team leader from being suspected of wrongdoing.
markingPoints: Works within authority limits and gets approval; no splitting of orders
Uses approved suppliers and fair, recorded choices
Refuses gifts and declares conflicts of interest
Keeps written, numbered records that can be checked
Explains why the rules protect the Centre and the leader

essays.stem: The supplier cannot provide the steel grade or section given on the drawing. Explain what you would do and why.
essays.modelAnswer: I first ask the supplier when the specified item will be in stock and whether another approved supplier has it, because the best answer is to get what was specified. If it cannot be found in time, I find out what the supplier can offer instead, with its exact size, grade and certificates. I do not accept a different grade or section myself, because it may be weaker, may weld differently, may need a different procedure or filler, or may not fit the other parts. I take the details to the engineer or person responsible for the design and ask for written approval. If the change is approved, I update the order, the drawing or a change note, the cutting list and, if needed, the WPS, and tell the team. If it is not approved, I tell the supervisor about the delay so the programme can be changed. The approval and changes are kept in the job file.
markingPoints: Tries to get the specified item first from other approved sources
Gets full details of the offered substitute
Does not accept it without approval, and explains the risks
Gets written approval and updates order, drawing, cutting list and WPS
Reports delays if not approved and files the records

essays.stem: Explain how you would review the materials ordered and used on a finished job, and how you would use the results to improve future ordering.
essays.modelAnswer: After the job I compare what was ordered with what was used. I list the steel, consumables and paint ordered, then count what is left over and what was scrapped, and work out the waste as a percentage for each type. I look at the reasons: a poor cutting plan, mistakes in cutting, design changes, damaged deliveries or over-ordering. I also check the deliveries: were they on time, complete and correct, and how quickly did suppliers fix problems. I compare the actual cost with the budget. I write a short report with the findings and agree actions with the team, such as better nesting of plate, a different waste allowance, ordering certain items earlier, or changing a supplier who was often late. Useful offcuts are labelled and booked into stock so they can be used on the next job. The waste figures and supplier records are kept, so the next estimate is based on real figures rather than guesses.
markingPoints: Compares ordered with used and works out waste
Finds the causes of waste or shortage
Reviews supplier performance and actual cost against budget
Agrees improvement actions and reports them
Books usable offcuts into stock and keeps records for future estimates

practical1.title: Produce a cutting list, a cutting plan and a priced, approved purchase order for a fabrication job
practical1.brief: The assessor gives your group the drawings of a small fabrication job (for example a steel staircase or a gate and fence panel), price lists or quotations from three suppliers (with made-up J$ prices, delivery charges and lead times), the job start date and a materials budget. The assessor tells you the GCT rate to use. As a group: make a cutting list from the drawings; plan how the pieces come out of 6 m lengths and nest any plate parts on a sheet sketch; add a waste allowance; estimate the electrodes or wire, discs and primer needed, showing the working; compare the three suppliers in a table and choose one, giving reasons; and write a purchase requisition and a purchase order with full descriptions, quantities, prices, delivery charges, GCT and the delivery date. One member plays the supervisor who approves the order and must be shown that it is within budget. Each member is responsible for one part of the work and checks another member's part. Photograph each stage and add the photos and documents to the group's practical.
materials: Drawings of a small fabrication job, a job start date and a materials budget
Price lists or quotations from three suppliers, with J$ prices, delivery charges and lead times (made up by the assessor)
Steel section tables with mass per metre
Cutting list, cutting plan, comparison table, requisition and purchase order forms
Calculators, rulers, pencils, and a computer with a spreadsheet if available
photos: The group sharing out the work
The cutting plan for 6 m lengths and the plate nesting sketch
The consumables and paint estimate with working shown
The supplier comparison table with the choice and reasons
The completed requisition and purchase order
The role-played approval, with the budget check
checklist: Took a full part in the group's work and checked another member's part
Made an accurate cutting list from the drawings
Planned cuts and nesting to keep waste low and ordered the right number of lengths or sheets
Worked out consumables and paint correctly, with working shown
Compared suppliers on price, delivery, lead time and terms and gave sound reasons
Wrote full, correct descriptions and quantities on the order
Worked out the totals, delivery and GCT correctly
Showed the order was within budget and got it approved by the right person
safety: Keep supplier prices and the Centre's budget figures confidential
Treat each other with respect during the approval role play
Keep cables and bags clear of walkways if computers are used
Take short breaks from close paperwork and screen work

practical2.title: Receive and check a delivery for a coded job, deal with problems, store it and update the stock records
practical2.brief: The assessor sets up a delivery in the Centre's store: steel lengths and plates with mill certificates, packets of electrodes, a spool of wire and a gas cylinder, with a delivery note and the purchase order. Some problems are planted: for example a short count, a wrong thickness, a heat number that does not match its certificate, and a damaged packet of electrodes. As a group, plan the unloading and checks and give each member a task. Count and measure everything against the order and delivery note, check heat numbers against the certificates, and check the condition of the consumables. Record every problem on the delivery note before signing, quarantine and label the failed items, and write a discrepancy report and a returns note. Store the accepted items correctly: steel on racks labelled with the job and heat number, low-hydrogen electrodes in the holding oven, and the cylinder upright and chained in the right store. Finally update the bin cards or the stock spreadsheet and work out the new reorder level for one consumable from figures the assessor gives. Photograph each stage and add the photos and documents to the group's practical.
materials: Steel lengths and plates with mill certificates, a delivery note and purchase order, with planted problems
Packets of electrodes (one damaged), a spool of wire and a gas cylinder
Tape measures, vernier calipers and a steel rule
Quarantine labels, job and heat number labels, marker pens
Goods received note, discrepancy report, returns note, bin cards or a stock spreadsheet
Gloves, safety boots, and lifting equipment or a trolley for heavy items
photos: The group's plan for unloading and checking
A member measuring plate thickness with a vernier
A heat number being compared with its mill certificate
The delivery note with problems recorded before signing
The accepted steel racked and labelled, electrodes in the oven and the cylinder chained
The completed discrepancy report, returns note and updated stock records
checklist: Helped plan the checks and carried out their task
Counted and measured items accurately against the order and delivery note
Checked heat numbers against certificates and found the planted problems
Recorded problems on the delivery note before signing
Quarantined and labelled failed items and wrote a clear discrepancy report and returns note
Stored steel, electrodes and the gas cylinder correctly
Worked out the reorder level correctly
safety: Wear gloves and safety boots when handling steel; watch for sharp edges and burrs
Carry long lengths with two people, one at each end, or use a trolley; lift heavy items with help or equipment
Keep gas cylinders upright and chained; move them only with a cylinder trolley
Keep the store tidy and walkways clear while unloading
